region_scene_page.compact: The early lane where R&B and gospel-rooted singing become broad pop through hooks, strings, dance rhythm, and unmistakable lead voices.
region_scene_page.standard: Early soul-pop crossover sits between first-wave rock and the later soul/funk universe. Ray Charles, Sam Cooke, Jackie Wilson, Ben E. King, Etta James, The Isley Brothers, early Motown, and related records show how Black R&B and gospel language entered mass pop without losing emotional pressure. Compared with doo-wop or teen-idol pop, the lead voice carries more church-derived urgency, the groove is heavier, and the arrangement often balances raw feeling with pop elegance.
